newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi cbank plans new interbank settlement system.
newsitem.headline: Saudi cbank plans new interbank settlement system.

text.p: The Saudi Arabian Monetary Agency (SAMA) plans to introduce an interbank settlement system this month to meet what it expects to be "phenomenal growth" in Saudi banking in the next decade, Governor Hamad Saud al-Sayyari said.
"The implementation phase of the EFT (Electronic Funds Transfer) system has now almost reached its conclusion with a go-live date of May 14," Sayyari told a conference in Riyadh.
A copy of his speech was obtained by Reuters on Tuesday.

"The system will give banks the ability to make and receive payments directly from their current accounts with SAMA on a real-time basis and provide immediate and final payment to recipients," he said of the system, to be known as SARIE, or the Saudi Arabian Riyal Interbank Express.
Until its launch, interbank settlement would continue to be carried out through cheque clearing or through telexed account transfers at SAMA's head office and branches.
"The banking system in Saudi Arabia is poised for phenomenal growth in the next decade," the governor said.
"The percentage of the banked population is set to grow dramatically following the provision of advanced payment systems including the new EFT system," he added, but gave no figures.
Sayyari said almost half the Saudi population was under 15.

"These young customers, being more educated in the ways of electronics, will be even more demanding of the banks in the services required. These will be the customers who... will make up the volume business for the future Smart cards."
Sayyari said SAMA had just finished research on introducing Smart cards, the stored-value cards which resemble credit cards but contain a computer chip that can effectively store cash.
"The challenge now is to plan for a quantum leap in customer growth and manage it in an evolutionary manner, building on the infrastructure put in place by SAMA," he said.
